title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 98 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 520–522 (Night 98, continuing directly from nights-97), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 98 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. The infidels put Ḍawʾ al-Makān and the vizier Dandān in fetters, and the two, still taking the vanished “ascetic” for a holy man, blame their plight on having doubted him. Sharrukān, holding the cave with what is left of the army, hears that his brother has been taken; he fights a day of heavy slaughter, loses thirty-five of his emirs, and decides to hold the cave's mouth in hope that the ascetic will bring help. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الثَّامِنَةُ وَالتِّسْعُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-thāminatu wa-al-tisʿūna
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the eighth-and-ninetieth,
sentences.i: And when it was the ninety-eighth night,

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّ الْكُفَّارَ لَمَّا قَبَضُوا عَلَى الْمَلِكِ ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ وَالْوَزِيرِ دَنْدَانَ قَالُوا لَهُمَا هَلْ مَعَكُمَا غَيْرُكُمَا فَنَقْبِضَ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-kuffāra lammā qabaḍū ʿalā al-maliki ḍawʾi al-makāni wa-al-wazīri dandāna qālū lahumā hal maʿakumā ghayrukumā fa-naqbiḍa ʿalayhi
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that the infidels, when they had seized upon King Ḍawʾ al-Makān and the vizier Dandān, said to the two of them: Is there with you-two other-than you-two, so that we may seize upon him?
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that when the infidels had laid hands on King Ḍawʾ al-Makān and the vizier Dandān, they asked them, “Is there anyone else with you, so that we may seize him too?”
sentences.n: qabaḍa ʿalā, “lay hold on, arrest”: the verb chooses the ʿalā. fa-naqbiḍa is subjunctive, because the fa- answers a question: “so that we may seize him.”

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ أَمَا تَرَوْنَ هَذَا الرَّجُلَ الْآخَرَ الَّذِي مَعَنَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-wazīru dandānu a-mā tarawna hādhā al-rajula al-ākhara alladhī maʿanā
sentences.l: And the vizier Dandān said: Do you not see this man, the other, who is with us?
sentences.i: The vizier Dandān said, “Do you not see this other man who is with us?”
sentences.n: a-mā, the question-alif with mā, “do … not?”, expects the answer yes. He means the ascetic, who is the old woman in disguise and has just handed them over.

sentences.t: قَالُوا وَحَقِّ الْمَسِيحِ وَالرُّهْبَانِ وَالْجَاثَلِيقِ وَالْمِطْرَانِ إِنَّنَا مَا نَرَى أَحَدًا غَيْرَكُمَا
sentences.tr: qālū wa-ḥaqqi al-masīḥi wa-al-ruhbāni wa-al-jāthalīqi wa-al-miṭrāni innanā mā narā aḥadan ghayrakumā
sentences.l: They said: By the right of the Messiah, and the monks, and the catholicos, and the metropolitan, we do not see anyone other-than you-two.
sentences.i: They said, “By the Messiah, by the monks, the catholicos and the metropolitan, we see no one but the two of you.”
sentences.n: wa-ḥaqqi, “by the right of”, is an oath; the wa- of swearing puts what follows in the genitive. al-jāthalīq is the catholicos, the head of an eastern church, and al-miṭrān the metropolitan bishop: the infidels swear by their own clergy.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْكُفَّارَ قَدْ وَضَعُوا الْقُيُودَ فِي أَرْجُلِهِمَا وَوَكَّلُوا بِهِمَا مَنْ يَحْرُسُهُمَا فِى الْمَبِيتِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-kuffāra qad waḍaʿū al-quyūda fī arjulihimā wa-wakkalū bihimā man yaḥrusuhumā fī al-mabīti
sentences.l: Then the infidels had put the fetters on their legs, and set-in-charge over the-two of them one who would guard the-two of them in the night-quarters.
sentences.i: Then the infidels put fetters on their legs and set someone over them to guard them through the night.
sentences.n: wakkala bi-, “put someone in charge of”: the verb chooses the bi-; bihimā is “over the two of them”. al-mabīt is the place or time of passing the night.

sentences.t: وَغَابَتِ الْعَجُوزُ ذَاتُ الدَّوَاهِي عَنْ أَعْيُنِهِمَا فَصَارَا يَتَأَسَّفَانِ وَيَقُولَانِ لِبَعْضِهِمَا إِنَّ الِاعْتِرَاضَ عَلَى الصَّالِحِينَ يُؤَدِّي إِلَى أَكْثَرَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ وَجَزَانَا مَا حَلَّ بِنَا مِنَ الضِّيقِ الَّذِي نَحْنُ فِيهِ
sentences.tr: wa-ghābati al-ʿajūzu dhātu al-dawāhī ʿan aʿyunihimā fa-ṣārā yataʾassafāni wa-yaqūlāni li-baʿḍihimā inna al-iʿtirāḍa ʿalā al-ṣāliḥīna yuʾaddī ilā akthara min dhālika wa-jazānā mā ḥalla binā mina al-ḍīqi alladhī naḥnu fīhi
sentences.l: And the old-woman Dhāt al-Dawāhī vanished from the eyes of the-two of them, and the-two began to grieve and to say to one-another: The objecting against the righteous leads to more than that; and what has alighted at us, of the strait that we are in, has requited us.
sentences.i: And the old woman, Dhāt al-Dawāhī, vanished from their sight. The two of them fell to lamenting, and said to each other, “To find fault with the righteous leads to worse than this; the straits we are in now are our just reward.”
sentences.n: The print has لبعضها, “to some of her”, a misprint for لبعضهما, “to each other (the two)”, corrected here. They still take the “ascetic” for a holy man, and think they are punished for having doubted him. jazānā is the verb jazā, “requite”, with “us” as object; its subject is mā ḥalla binā, “what has come down upon us”. It could also be the noun jazāʾunā, “our recompense”, written without its hamza.

sentences.t: هَذَا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ وَالْوَزِيرِ دَنْدَانَ
sentences.tr: hādhā mā kāna min amri ḍawʾi al-makāni wa-al-wazīri dandāna
sentences.l: This is what was of the affair of Ḍawʾ al-Makān and the vizier Dandān.
sentences.i: So much for Ḍawʾ al-Makān and the vizier Dandān.
sentences.n: The print has الوزيز, a misprint for الوزير, “the vizier”, corrected here. hādhā mā kāna min amri … is the storyteller's formula for leaving one thread and taking up another.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ الْمَلِكِ شَرْكَانَ فَإِنَّهُ بَاتَ تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةَ فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ الصَّبَاحُ قَامَ وَصَلَّى صَلَٰوةَ الصُّبْحِ ثُمَّ نَهَضَ هُوَ وَمَنْ مَعَهُ مِنَ الْعَسَاكِرِ وَتَأَهَّبُوا إِلَى قِتَالِ الْكُفَّارِ وَقَوَّى قَلْبَهُمْ شَرْكَانُ وَوَعَدَهُمْ بِكُلِّ خَيْرٍ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā mā kāna min amri al-maliki sharrukāna fa-innahu bāta tilka al-laylata fa-lammā aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu qāma wa-ṣallā ṣalāta al-ṣubḥi thumma nahaḍa huwa wa-man maʿahu mina al-ʿasākiri wa-taʾahhabū ilā qitāli al-kuffāri wa-qawwā qalbahum sharrukānu wa-waʿadahum bi-kulli khayrin
sentences.l: And as for what was of the affair of King Sharrukān, he passed that night; and when the morning morninged, he rose and prayed the prayer of the dawn; then he arose, he and whoever was with him of the troops, and they made-ready for the fighting of the infidels; and Sharrukān strengthened their heart and promised them every good.
sentences.i: As for King Sharrukān, he passed that night, and when morning came he rose and said the dawn prayer. Then he set out with the troops who were with him, and they made ready to fight the infidels; Sharrukān put heart into them and promised them every good thing.
sentences.n: aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu, “the morning became morning”, plays verb against its own noun. The print spells ṣalāt as صلوة, the old spelling with wāw. waʿada bi-, “promise”: the verb chooses the bi- of the thing promised.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ سَارُوا إِلَى أَنْ وَصَلُوا إِلَى الْكُفَّارِ فَلَمَّا رَأٰهُمُ الْكُفَّارُ مِنْ بَعِيدٍ قَالُوا لَهُمْ يَا مُسْلِمُونَ إِنَّا أَسَرْنَا سُلْطَانَكُمْ وَوَزِيرَهُ الَّذِي بِهِ انْتِظَامُ أَمْرِكُمْ
sentences.tr: thumma sārū ilā an waṣalū ilā al-kuffāri fa-lammā raʾāhumu al-kuffāru min baʿīdin qālū lahum yā muslimūna innā asarnā sulṭānakum wa-wazīrahu alladhī bihi intiẓāmu amrikum
sentences.l: Then they went until they reached the infidels; and when the infidels saw them from afar, they said to them: O Muslims, we have captured your sultan and his vizier, by whom is the ordering of your affair.
sentences.i: Then they marched until they came up with the infidels. When the infidels saw them from far off they called out, “Muslims! We have taken your sultan prisoner, and his vizier too, on whom the good order of your affairs depends.
sentences.n: The print has ووزيرة, a misprint for ووزيره, “and his vizier”, corrected here. It spells raʾāhum as رأهم, without the long ā. bihi intiẓāmu amrikum, “by him is the ordering of your affair”: the vizier is what holds the state together.

sentences.t: وَإِنْ لَمْ تَرْجِعُوا عَنْ قِتَالِنَا قَتَلْنَاكُمْ عَنْ آخِرِكُمْ وَإِذَا سَلَّمْتُمْ لَنَا أَنْفُسَكُمْ فَإِنَّنَا نَرُوحُ بِكُمْ إِلَى مَلِكِنَا فَيُصَالِحُكُمْ عَلَى أَنْ لَا تَخْرُجُوا مِنْ بِلَادِنَا وَلَا تَذْهَبُوا إِلَى بِلَادِكُمْ وَلَا تَضُرُّونَا بِشَيْءٍ وَلَا نَضُرَّكُمْ بِشَيْءٍ
sentences.tr: wa-in lam tarjiʿū ʿan qitālinā qatalnākum ʿan ākhirikum wa-idhā sallamtum lanā anfusakum fa-innanā narūḥu bikum ilā malikinā fa-yuṣāliḥukum ʿalā an lā takhrujū min bilādinā wa-lā tadhhabū ilā bilādikum wa-lā taḍurrūnā bi-shayʾin wa-lā naḍurrakum bi-shayʾin
sentences.l: And if you do not turn back from fighting us, we will kill you to the last of you; and if you surrender to us your selves, we will go with you to our king, and he will make-peace with you on condition that you do not go out from our lands, nor go to your lands, nor harm us with anything, nor we harm you with anything.
sentences.i: If you do not give up fighting us, we will kill you to the last man. But if you surrender yourselves to us, we will take you to our king, and he will make peace with you, on condition that you do not leave our country or go back to your own, and that you do us no harm and we do you none.
sentences.n: ʿan ākhirikum, “to the last of you”: every one. rāḥa bi-, “go with”, is “take”: the verb chooses the bi-. The terms, as printed, would keep the Muslims in the Christians' country for good. taḍurrūnā and naḍurrakum are subjunctive after an lā: taḍurrū-nā, “(that) you harm us”.

sentences.t: فَإِنْ طَابَ خَاطِرُكُمْ كَانَ الْحَظُّ لَكُمْ وَإِنْ أَبَيْتُمْ فَمَا يَكُونُ إِلَّاقَتْلُكُمْ وَقَدْ عَرَّفْنَاكُمْ وَهَذَا آخِرُ كَلَامِنَا مَعَكُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-in ṭāba khāṭirukum kāna al-ḥaẓẓu lakum wa-in abaytum fa-mā yakūnu illā qatlukum wa-qad ʿarrafnākum wa-hādhā ākhiru kalāminā maʿakum
sentences.l: And if your mind is pleased, the good-fortune will be yours; and if you refuse, there will not be anything except your killing. And we have let-you-know, and this is the last of our speech with you.
sentences.i: If you are content with that, the luck is yours; if you refuse, it will be nothing but your death. We have told you, and this is our last word to you.”
sentences.n: The print runs illā qatlukum together as one word, الاقتلكم; the spacing is kept. ṭāba khāṭirukum, “your mind is good”, is “you agree, you are content”. ʿarrafnākum, form II, “we have made known to you”: we have told you. The unpointed print could also be read ʿarafnākum, “we know you”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ شَرْكَانُ كَلَامَهُمْ وَتَحَقَّقَ أَسْرَ أَخِيهِ وَالْوَزِيرِ دَنْدَانَ عَظُمَ عَلَيْهِ ذَلِكَ وَبَكَى وَضَعُفَتْ قُوَّتُهُ وَأَيْقَنَ بِالْهَلَاكِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa sharrukānu kalāmahum wa-taḥaqqaqa asra akhīhi wa-al-wazīri dandāna ʿaẓuma ʿalayhi dhālika wa-bakā wa-ḍaʿufat quwwatuhu wa-ayqana bi-al-halāki
sentences.l: And when Sharrukān heard their speech and made-certain of the capture of his brother and the vizier Dandān, that was great upon him, and he wept, and his strength weakened, and he was certain of the perishing.
sentences.i: When Sharrukān heard what they said, and knew for certain that his brother and the vizier Dandān had been taken, it weighed on him heavily. He wept, his strength failed him, and he was sure that he would perish.
sentences.n: ʿaẓuma ʿalayhi, “it was great upon him”: it grieved him sorely. ayqana bi-, “be certain of”: the verb chooses the bi-.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ فِي نَفْسِهِ يَا تُرَى مَا سَبَبُ أَسْرِهِمَا هَلْ حَصَلَ مِنْهُمَا إِسَاءَةُ أَدَبٍ فِي حَقِّ الزَّاهِدِ وَاعْتَرَضَا عَلَيْهِ أَوْ مَا شَأْنُهُمَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla fī nafsihi yā turā mā sababu asrihimā hal ḥaṣala minhumā isāʾatu adabin fī ḥaqqi al-zāhidi wa-iʿtaraḍā ʿalayhi aw mā shaʾnuhumā
sentences.l: And he said in his soul: O, is it seen, what is the cause of their capture? Did there occur from the-two of them an ill-doing of manners in the right of the ascetic, and did they object against him? Or what is their case?
sentences.i: He said to himself, “What, I wonder, was the cause of their capture? Did they fail in respect toward the ascetic and find fault with him? Or what has happened to them?”
sentences.n: yā turā, “O, is it seen?”, is the colloquial “I wonder”. Like his brother, Sharrukān still believes in the ascetic.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ نَهَضُوا إِلَى قِتَالِ الْكُفَّارِ فَقَتَلُوا مِنْهُمْ خَلْقًا كَثِيرًا وَتَبَيَّنَ فِي ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمِ الشُّجَاعُ مِنَ الْجَبَانِ وَاخْتَضَبَ السَّيْفُ وَالسِّنَانُ وَتَهَافَتَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْكُفَّارُ تَهَافُتَ الذُّبَابِ عَلَى الشَّرَابِ مِنْ كُلِّ مَكَانٍ
sentences.tr: thumma nahaḍū ilā qitāli al-kuffāri fa-qatalū minhum khalqan kathīran wa-tabayyana fī dhālika al-yawmi al-shujāʿu mina al-jabāni wa-ikhtaḍaba al-sayfu wa-al-sinānu wa-tahāfata ʿalayhimu al-kuffāru tahāfuta al-dhubābi ʿalā al-sharābi min kulli makānin
sentences.l: Then they rose to the fighting of the infidels, and they killed of them a great creation; and on that day the brave was made-clear from the coward, and the sword and the spearhead were dyed; and the infidels swarmed upon them, the swarming of the flies upon the drink, from every place.
sentences.i: Then they went out to fight the infidels and killed a great many of them. That day showed the brave apart from the coward; sword and spearhead were dyed with blood; and the infidels swarmed in on them from every side, as flies swarm onto a drink.
sentences.n: khalqan kathīran, “a great creation”, is “a great many”. Sajʿ: al-jabāni/al-sinānu. ikhtaḍaba, “be dyed”, is used of henna; here the dye is blood.

sentences.t: وَمَا زَالَ شَرْكَانُ وَمَنْ مَعَهُ يُقَاتِلُونَ قِتَالَ مَنْ لَا يَخَافُ الْمَوْتَ وَلَا يَعْتَرِيهِ فِي طَلَبِ الْفُرْصَةِ فَوْتٌ حَتَّى سَالَ الْوَادِي بِالدِّمَاءِ وَامْتَلَائَتِ الْأَرْضُ بِالْقَتْلَى
sentences.tr: wa-mā zāla sharrukānu wa-man maʿahu yuqātilūna qitāla man lā yakhāfu al-mawta wa-lā yaʿtarīhi fī ṭalabi al-furṣati fawtun ḥattā sāla al-wādī bi-al-dimāʾi wa-imtalaʾati al-arḍu bi-al-qatlā
sentences.l: And Sharrukān and whoever was with him did not cease fighting the fighting of one who does not fear the death, and to whom no missing comes in the seeking of the chance, until the valley flowed with the bloods and the earth was filled with the slain.
sentences.i: Sharrukān and his men fought on like men who do not fear death and never miss their chance, until the valley ran with blood and the ground was covered with the slain.
sentences.n: Sajʿ: al-mawta/fawtun. qitāla man …, “the fighting of one who …”, is a cognate accusative: the noun of the verb's own root says how they fought. sāla bi-, “flow with”: bi- of what fills it, as in imtalaʾat bi-. The print spells imtalaʾat as امتلائت.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَقْبَلَ اللَّيْلُ تَفَرَّقَتِ الْجُيُوشُ وَكُلٌّ مِنَ الْفَرِيقَيْنِ ذَهَبَ إِلَى مَكَانِهِ وَعَادَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ إِلَى تِلْكَ الْمَغَارَةِ وَبَانَتْ مِنْهُمُ الْغَلَبَةُ وَالْخَسَارَةُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aqbala al-laylu tafarraqati al-juyūshu wa-kullun mina al-farīqayni dhahaba ilā makānihi wa-ʿāda al-muslimūna ilā tilka al-maghārati wa-bānat minhumu al-ghalabatu wa-al-khasāratu
sentences.l: And when the night came-on, the armies separated, and each of the two parties went to its place; and the Muslims returned to that cave, and there appeared from them the being-overcome and the loss.
sentences.i: When night came on, the armies drew apart, each side to its own ground. The Muslims went back to the cave, and it was plain that they had been worsted and had suffered loss.
sentences.n: al-ghalaba is “overpowering”; with minhum, “from them”, it is the defeat they suffered, not a victory they won. Sajʿ: al-maghārati/al-khasāratu.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَبْقَ مِنْهُمْ إِلَّا الْقَلِيلُ لَمْ يَكُنْ مِنْهُمْ إِلَّا عَلَى اللَّهِ وَالسَّيْفِ تَعْوِيلٌ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yabqa minhum illā al-qalīlu lam yakun minhum illā ʿalā allāhi wa-al-sayfi taʿwīlun
sentences.l: And there did not remain of them except the few; there was not from them, except upon God and the sword, a relying.
sentences.i: Only a few of them were left, and they had nothing to rely on but God and the sword.
sentences.n: taʿwīl ʿalā, “reliance on”, comes last for the rhyme with al-qalīlu: the sentence is built backwards so that the noun ends it.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ قُتِلَ مِنْهُمْ فِي هَذَا النَّهَارِ خَمْسَةٌ وَثَلَٰثُونَ فَارِسًا مِنَ الْأُمَرَاءِ الْأَعْيَانِ وَإِنْ قُتِلَ بِسَيْفِهِمْ مِنَ الْكُفَّارِ آلَافٌ مِنَ الرِّجَالِ وَالرُّكْبَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-qad qutila minhum fī hādhā al-nahāri khamsatun wa-thalāthūna fārisan mina al-umarāʾi al-aʿyāni wa-in qutila bi-sayfihim mina al-kuffāri ālāfun mina al-rijāli wa-al-rukbāni
sentences.l: And there had been killed of them on this day five-and-thirty horsemen of the emirs, the notables, even if there were killed by their sword, of the infidels, thousands of the men-on-foot and the riders.
sentences.i: That day thirty-five horsemen had been killed among them, emirs and men of rank, though their swords had killed thousands of the infidels, on foot and mounted.
sentences.n: The dagger alif on ثلٰثون is the print's own. wa-in, “even if, although”, introduces the set-off: their own losses were few in number but grievous. al-rijāl here are the foot-soldiers, against al-rukbān, the riders; sajʿ: al-aʿyāni/al-rukbāni.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا عَايَنَ شَرْكَانُ ذَلِكَ ضَاقَ عَلَيْهِ الْأَمْرُ وَقَالَ لِأَصْحَابِهِ كَيْفَ الْعَمَلُ فَقَالَ لَهُ أَصْحَابُهُ لَايَكُونُ إِلَّا مَايُرِيدُهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ʿāyana sharrukānu dhālika ḍāqa ʿalayhi al-amru wa-qāla li-aṣḥābihi kayfa al-ʿamalu fa-qāla lahu aṣḥābuhu lā yakūnu illā mā yurīduhu allāhu taʿālā
sentences.l: And when Sharrukān beheld that, the affair grew-narrow upon him, and he said to his companions: How is the doing? And his companions said to him: There will not be except what God the Exalted wills.
sentences.i: When Sharrukān saw this, he was hard pressed, and said to his companions, “What is to be done?” They answered, “Nothing will happen but what God Most High wills.”
sentences.n: The print runs lā yakūnu and mā yurīduhu together as one word each, لايكون and مايريده; the spacing is kept. ḍāqa ʿalayhi al-amru, “the affair grew narrow on him”: he was in straits. kayfa al-ʿamalu, “how is the doing?”, is the Nights' stock “what is to be done?”

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَ ثَانِي يَوْمٍ قَالَ شَرْكَانُ لِبَقِيَّةِ الْعَسْكَرِإِنْ خَرَجْتُمْ لِلْقِتَالِ مَا بَقِيَ مِنْكُمْ أَحَدٌ لِأَنَّهُ لَمْ يَبْقَ عِنْدَنَا إِلَّا قَلِيلٌ مِنَ الْمَاءِ وَالزَّادِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kāna thānī yawmin qāla sharrukānu li-baqiyyati al-ʿaskari in kharajtum li-al-qitāli mā baqiya minkum aḥadun li-annahu lam yabqa ʿindanā illā qalīlun mina al-māʾi wa-al-zādi
sentences.l: And when it was the second of a day, Sharrukān said to the remainder of the army: If you go out to the fighting, there will not remain of you anyone; for there has not remained with us except a little of the water and the provision.
sentences.i: On the next day Sharrukān said to what was left of the army, “If you go out to fight, not one of you will be left. And we have only a little water and food left.
sentences.n: The print runs al-ʿaskari in together as one word, العسكران; the spacing is kept, as in night 95. thānī yawmin, “the second of a day”, is “the next day”. li-annahu, “because”, gives the reason for the plan that follows: they cannot fight in the open, and they cannot wait long.

sentences.t: وَالرَّأْيُ الَّذِي عِنْدِى فِيهِ الرَّشَادُ أَنْ تُجَرِّدُوا سُيُوفَكُمْ وَتَخْرُجُوا وَتَقِفُوا عَلَى بَابِ تِلْكَ الْمَغَارَةِ لِأَجْلِ أَنْ تَدْفَعُوا عَنْ أَنْفُسِكُمْ مَنْ يَدْخُلُ عَلَيْكُمْ
sentences.tr: wa-al-raʾyu alladhī ʿindī fīhi al-rashādu an tujarridū suyūfakum wa-takhrujū wa-taqifū ʿalā bābi tilka al-maghārati li-ajli an tadfaʿū ʿan anfusikum man yadkhulu ʿalaykum
sentences.l: And the opinion that is with me, in which is the right-guidance, is that you bare your swords and go out and stand at the door of that cave, for the sake of that you push away from your selves whoever comes in upon you.
sentences.i: The sound plan, as I see it, is this: draw your swords, go out, and hold the mouth of the cave, so that you can beat off from yourselves anyone who tries to come in at you.
sentences.n: The shadda on تجرّدوا is the print's own: tujarridū, form II, “strip, bare (a sword)”. li-ajli an, “for the sake of that”, is “so that”, with the subjunctive. dakhala ʿalā, “come in upon”, is to enter where someone is, here as an attacker.

sentences.t: فَلَعَلَّ الزَّاهِدَ أَنْ يَكُونَ وَصَلَ إِلَى عَسْكَرِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَيَأْتِينَا بِعَشَرَةِ آلَافِ فَارِسٍ فَيُعِينُونَنَا عَلَى قِتَالِ الْكَفَرَةِ وَلَعَلَّ الْكُفَّارَ لَمْ يَنْظُرُوهُ هُوَ وَمَنْ مَعَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-laʿalla al-zāhida an yakūna waṣala ilā ʿaskari al-muslimīna wa-yaʾtīnā bi-ʿasharati ālāfi fārisin fa-yuʿīnūnanā ʿalā qitāli al-kafarati wa-laʿalla al-kuffāra lam yanẓurūhu huwa wa-man maʿahu
sentences.l: For perhaps the ascetic may have reached the army of the Muslims and will come to us with ten thousand horsemen, and they will help us in the fighting of the unbelievers; and perhaps the infidels did not see him, he and whoever is with him.”
sentences.i: Perhaps the ascetic has reached the Muslim army and will bring us ten thousand horsemen to help us fight the unbelievers; perhaps the infidels never saw him and those with him.”
sentences.n: The print has وبأنينا, a misprint for ويأتينا, “and will come to us”, corrected here. laʿalla … an yakūna, “perhaps … that he be”, puts an an where Classical usage has none after laʿalla. atā bi-, “come with”, is “bring”: the verb chooses the bi-. Sharrukān still trusts the ascetic, not knowing that the ascetic is the old woman who betrayed his brother and the vizier.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ أَصْحَابُهُ إِنَّ هَذَا الرَّأْىَ هُوَ الصَّوَابُ وَمَا فِي سَدَادِهِ ارْتِيَابٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu aṣḥābuhu inna hādhā al-raʾya huwa al-ṣawābu wa-mā fī sadādihi irtiyābun
sentences.l: And his companions said to him: This opinion, it is the right, and there is not in its soundness a doubting.
sentences.i: His companions said to him, “This plan is the right one, and there is no doubt that it is sound.”
sentences.n: Sajʿ: al-ṣawābu/irtiyābun. The print spells raʾy here with final ى, الرأى.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْعَسْكَرَ خَرَجُوا وَمَلَكُوا بَابَ الْمَغَارَةِ وَوَقَفُوا فِي طَرَفَيْهِ وَكُلُّ مَنْ أَرَادَ أَنْ يَدْخُلَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنَ الْكُفَّارِ يَقْتُلُونَهُ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-ʿaskara kharajū wa-malakū bāba al-maghārati wa-waqafū fī ṭarafayhi wa-kullu man arāda an yadkhula ʿalayhim mina al-kuffāri yaqtulūnahu
sentences.l: Then the army went out and held the door of the cave and stood at its two sides; and everyone who wanted to come in upon them of the infidels, they would kill him.
sentences.i: So the army went out, took the mouth of the cave and stood on either side of it, and any infidel who tried to get in at them they killed.
sentences.n: al-ʿaskar, “the army”, is singular but takes plural verbs, kharajū, malakū: the army is many men.

sentences.t: وَصَارُوا يَدْفَعُونَ الْكُفَّارَ عَنِ الْبَابِ وَصَبَرُوا عَلَى قِتَالِ الْكُفَّارِ إِلَى أَنْ ذَهَبَ النَّهَارُ وَأَقْبَلَ اللَّيْلُ بِالِاعْتِكَارِ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣārū yadfaʿūna al-kuffāra ʿani al-bābi wa-ṣabarū ʿalā qitāli al-kuffāri ilā an dhahaba al-nahāru wa-aqbala al-laylu bi-al-iʿtikāri
sentences.l: And they began to push the infidels from the door, and they endured in the fighting of the infidels until the day went and the night came-on with the darkening.
sentences.i: They kept driving the infidels back from the entrance, and held out in the fight until the day was gone and night came on in its darkness.
sentences.n: ṣabara ʿalā, “endure, hold out in”: the verb chooses the ʿalā. aqbala bi-, “come on with”: bi- of what it brings. Sajʿ: al-nahāru/al-iʿtikāri.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
